cvEn:
Shimon-Avner Levi, son of Mazal and Shabtai-Eliyahu, was born on the 4th of Iyar 5687 (6 May 1927). Details of his life are not known. From the age of 11 he was a member of the Betar youth movement, and from there he joined the Irgun underground, where his comrades knew him by the name "Rav-Samal Avner" (Staff Sergeant Avner). He was consistent and ruthless as a fighter and knew no fear. For 16 months he was held in the Latrun prison, and he was released shortly before the outbreak of the War of Independence.

Shimon went out with his comrades to plant explosive charges at gathering places of gang members near the Jaffa Gate. After the first charge was successfully placed, the second exploded close to the vehicle he was riding in and hurled it against a stone wall. The members of the cell jumped out, and in the fire that was directed at them he was wounded and fell, on the 25th of Tevet 5708 (7 January 1948). He was buried on the Mount of Olives in Jerusalem. His name is engraved on the memorial erected at the Military Cemetery on Mount Herzl in memory of the fallen of the Jewish Quarter and of the fighters who fell in the battle for Jerusalem and were buried on the Mount of Olives.
